features.title: State layer as startup anchor
features.behavior: Cold-start for cross-module and resume tasks begins with current-status, current-sprint and release-status before local search.

verification.target: Read docs/current-status.md, docs/current-sprint.md and docs/release-status.md before local search.

features.residual_risk: State docs still need manual updates after each non-trivial task.

features.title: Lifecycle with focused validation
features.behavior: Each non-trivial task must record a local hypothesis, make a bounded edit and immediately run focused validation before widening scope.

verification.target: Use the lifecycle flow and confirm that the first post-edit action is a focused validation step.

features.residual_risk: Discipline is enforced by process and review, not by a runtime hook yet.

features.title: Task routing by mode
features.behavior: Research, implementation, review and release tasks are routed through explicit modes with different tool and output expectations.

verification.target: Classify the task against docs/agent-routing-matrix.md before expanding scope.

features.residual_risk: Routing still depends on operator discipline for ambiguous tasks.

features.title: Synthetic and real-folder end-to-end validation
features.behavior: Cross-module converter changes are verified through schema-backed run-package validation and end-to-end runs, not only unit tests.
features.residual_risk: Real-corpus E2E still requires a deliberate task decision and is not part of every CI run.

features.title: Machine-readable harness feature spine
features.behavior: Harness capabilities are tracked in a machine-readable file with behavior, state, verification and evidence instead of relying on narrative roadmap alone.
features.residual_risk: The spine currently covers the harness layer and not every product capability of the converter.

features.title: Bootstrap contract for cold start
features.behavior: A new session can reacquire the repo, environment, release scope and next validation path without broad search.
features.residual_risk: Bootstrap still depends on a healthy local .venv and Windows OCR prerequisites.

features.title: Clean exit checklist
features.behavior: Every non-trivial task ends with validation evidence, state updates, residual risk capture and resume breadcrumbs.
features.residual_risk: Checklist enforcement is procedural until a higher-level workflow hook is added.

features.title: Sprint contract template
features.behavior: Non-trivial tasks can declare goal, non-goals, local hypothesis, validation plan and stop conditions before edits begin.
features.residual_risk: The template exists, but adoption still depends on task complexity and operator judgment.

features.title: Evaluator rubric for completion quality
features.behavior: Task quality can be scored against scope control, validation, evidence and closeout instead of relying on subjective completion claims.
features.residual_risk: The rubric is defined and now feeds a generated weekly snapshot, but final qualitative judgement still needs human review.

features.title: Harness assets validator in CI
features.behavior: Core harness artifacts are validated in CI so regressions in feature spine or required process docs fail early.
features.residual_risk: The validator checks structure and file presence, not the semantic quality of every document.

features.title: Canonical document.v1 package
features.behavior: The main product output is a portable document.v1.json package with source metadata, processing route, semantic metadata, structural units, assets and quality flags instead of plain text only, plus root-level processed-documents-catalog JSON/XLSX indexes that map source names to output folders, statuses and operator hyperlinks, and first-class human-readable Markdown/HTML exports for operator QC.
features.residual_risk: Advanced PDF tables, formulas and figures now have heuristic unit extraction, but pixel-perfect table geometry and multimodal figure understanding remain downstream concerns.

features.title: DOCX native conversion route
features.behavior: DOCX files are processed natively with reading-order preservation, semantic units for headings, lists, captions, tables, formulas, headers, footers and footnotes, extracted media assets and search_text.txt.
features.residual_risk: DOCX headers, footers, footnotes and formulas are extracted heuristically from package XML; complex field codes and linked external objects may still need review.

features.title: DOCX converter package split
features.behavior: The legacy monolithic DOCX converter is split into smaller package modules for pipeline, inline glyph recognition and formula handling, while `doc_converter.converters.docx` keeps the previous public import surface through `__init__.py` re-exports.
features.residual_risk: Internal monkeypatch targets now need to point at concrete DOCX submodules when implementation imports helpers directly; remaining repo-wide file-size debt now sits outside the DOCX slice in formula_benchmark.py.

features.title: Runner orchestration package split
features.behavior: Conversion orchestration, startup path validation, resume reuse, processed catalog generation and formula postprocess live in `doc_converter.run` modules, while `doc_converter.runner` stays a thin compatibility wrapper for the public API used by CLI, GUI and tests.
features.residual_risk: Internal monkeypatch targets for runner internals now need to point at concrete `doc_converter.run` submodules when implementation imports helpers directly; remaining repo-wide file-size debt is now concentrated in formula_benchmark.py.

features.title: Shared PDF table parser package
features.behavior: Dominant-width inference, continuation merge and `table_structure_warning` normalization live in `doc_converter.tables`, and both `pdf_text` and `pdf_scan` routes import the same table parser instead of owning separate or converter-local heuristics.
features.residual_risk: Shared parser logic is centralized, but table unit assembly and richer semantics still remain route-local; next backlog is no longer parser drift, but warning density, negative/control contour and scan OCR blocker handling.

features.title: Converter protocol and route registry
features.behavior: Inventory route detection and run orchestration dispatch both flow through a shared `doc_converter.converters` registry with `ConverterProtocol` adapters, so future converter registration no longer requires hard-coded imports or route branches inside orchestration.
features.residual_risk: Stable manifest and document schemas still enumerate the current product formats, so architecture-only demo converters should stay opt-in and isolate schema validation unless the public format contract is intentionally expanded.

features.title: PDF text-layer conversion route
features.behavior: PDF files with an extractable text layer are processed without OCR using layout-first extraction, page provenance, repeated edge-block filtering into header/footer units and heuristic table/formula/figure unit extraction.
features.residual_risk: PDF table/formula/figure extraction is heuristic over text blocks; exact cell geometry, figure pixels and multimodal semantics remain downstream/review concerns.

features.title: PDF scan OCR route
features.behavior: PDF scans are processed through OCR into searchable.pdf and sidecar text, then emitted into canonical document packages with OCR provenance, quality flags and heuristic table/formula/figure units from OCR text.
features.residual_risk: Optional OCR helpers jbig2, pngquant and verapdf are not required and remain uninstalled by default.

features.title: XLSX native conversion route
features.behavior: XLSX workbooks are processed natively with worksheet sections, inferred sheet tables, row and cell units, structured cell payloads, preserved Excel formulas and cached formula values where present.
features.residual_risk: The converter preserves Excel formulas and cached workbook values but does not recalculate formulas; downstream calculation still needs an Excel-compatible formula engine or recalculation step.

features.title: Formula recognition provider and local backend env config
features.behavior: Converter runtime auto-loads formula recognition settings from `.env.local`/`.env` plus process environment overrides, supporting explicit `FORMULA_RECOGNITION_*` keys, shorthand aliases like `LLM_PROVIDER`, provider-specific model keys and `FORMULA_MODEL`, plus optional `FORMULA_RECOGNITION_LOCAL_BACKEND=tesseract`; when OpenRouter credentials are present and no dedicated formula override is set, the formula slice defaults to `openrouter` + `openai/gpt-4o`, while run metadata stores only configured `provider`/`model`/`local_backend` fields and never serializes the secret itself.
features.residual_risk: The env loader searches the current working directory and its ancestors; if the converter is launched from an unrelated directory, the operator must export the variables explicitly or start the command from the project tree. The default formula model is tuned for multimodal OCR-like extraction, while the current local backend depends on Windows Tesseract availability and should remain an opt-in fallback rather than a deterministic benchmark baseline.

features.title: Formula image recognition postprocess
features.behavior: When formula recognition is configured, runner reopens each canonical `document.v1.json`, scans `formula_image` units and residual `formula` units that still lack a machine-readable contract (currently: no usable `calc_expr`), first tries local WMF/MathType hint extraction, then an optional local OCR backend and only after that falls back to an OpenRouter multimodal call for unresolved assets, requesting strict `json_schema` output and writing successful results back into `unit.text`, `unit.formula`, `processing.formula_recognition` and a sidecar `formula-recognition.jsonl` artifact.
features.residual_risk: Automated validation uses mocked provider responses and does not spend real OpenRouter credits; live quality still depends on provider availability, model behavior, local Tesseract availability and successful rasterization of WMF/EMF assets on Windows.

features.title: Data-driven known MathType formula patterns
features.behavior: Known MathType/WMF formula recovery rules, noisy linear-text recovery and full formula representations live in versioned JSON data with schema validation and package-data sync instead of being extended through a hard-coded Python condition table.
features.residual_risk: The JSON contract preserves existing signature predicates, including suffix checks, but future generalized WMF parser work still needs separate false-positive controls beyond known-pattern lookup.

features.title: Semantic document metadata block
features.behavior: Each canonical package includes rule-based title, document_type, short_summary, confidence and method fields without depending on an external LLM.
features.residual_risk: Rule-based classification still depends on corpus wording and may need new patterns on unseen document families.

features.title: Quality flags and review-required reporting
features.behavior: The converter emits normalized document and unit quality flags, review-required.jsonl, root-level processed-documents-catalog JSON/XLSX indexes and summary reason buckets for failed, partial and review-required cases.
features.residual_risk: Some quality signals remain heuristic and may need threshold tuning on new corpora.

features.title: Resume, dedup and queue-state reuse
features.behavior: Repeated runs reuse previous output for unchanged files, preserve duplicate provenance and keep queue-state stable instead of reprocessing blindly.
features.residual_risk: Resume behavior is validated within current local run layout and has not been generalized to distributed execution.

features.title: Chunking and downstream handoff
features.behavior: Structural units can be transformed into portability-safe chunks.v1.jsonl and handed downstream without re-running OCR or reparsing the source files.
features.residual_risk: DB mapping notes and downstream loaders still evolve separately from the converter runtime.

features.title: Stable downstream contract catalog
features.behavior: Downstream-facing artifacts have a stable v1 JSON Schema catalog, SHA-256 schema drift snapshots and focused tests for contract stability before consumers depend on them.
features.residual_risk: Stable v1 schema fingerprints protect contract drift, but downstream loaders still need their own compatibility tests against real consumer databases.

features.title: Run-level agent metadata contract
features.behavior: Each new run package carries required `agent_run_metadata` with agent identity and task traceability in `run.json`; CLI can pass explicit values and runner fills safe defaults for manual runs.
features.residual_risk: Historical run packages still need validator-side fallback metadata; raw direct schema validation of old `run.json` payloads remains intentionally strict.

features.title: Universal document package validator
features.behavior: A dedicated validation script walks a run directory, schema-checks every canonical `document.v1.json` and validates optional `formula-recognition.jsonl` sidecars, while `validate_run_package.py` remains legacy-compatible for old `run.json` payloads.
features.residual_risk: Validator output is currently aggregate-only; when a run contains many documents, deeper per-document diagnostics still rely on the first schema error and manual inspection.

features.title: Operator GUI and Windows release packaging
features.behavior: Operators can run the converter through a GUI with progress, current file, cancel, open output, HTML QC and summary counts, while Windows packaging produces a portable EXE and release zip.
features.residual_risk: Pause and resume are intentionally not exposed as GUI controls; the product relies on safe rerun semantics instead.

features.title: Structured CLI result envelope
features.behavior: CLI commands default to human-readable output, while `--output-format=json` emits a fixed `cli-result.v1` envelope with `command`, `status`, `exit_code`, `message` and command-specific `data`, so autonomous agents can react without parsing prose.
features.residual_risk: The envelope is stable, but command-specific `data` payloads still vary by subcommand until S6.2 adds a structured runtime event contract.

features.title: Structured environment doctor command
features.behavior: `document-converter doctor` reports OCR runtime, bundled font availability, schema availability and OpenRouter reachability through the same CLI envelope and returns `environment_invalid` when the runtime is not ready.
features.residual_risk: Bundled font checks are expected to stay red until S4.3, and OpenRouter reachability is only probed when provider configuration is present.

features.title: Inventory-only dry-run command
features.behavior: `document-converter dry-run` performs deterministic inventory and route classification without creating run directories, and returns supported/unsupported records plus route and warning counts through the structured CLI envelope.
features.residual_risk: Dry-run stops at inventory/classification and does not exercise per-route converter startup requirements; full `convert-folder` runs remain the conversion gate.

features.title: Structured runtime telemetry log
features.behavior: Every converter run emits a schema-backed `telemetry.jsonl` event stream through a central logger adapter, and `validate_run_package.py` validates `log.v1` alongside the rest of the run package.
features.residual_risk: Legacy `processing-log.jsonl` and `errors.jsonl` are still emitted as compatibility mirrors until a later operator-facing deprecation tranche removes them.

features.title: Input hardening for untrusted documents
features.behavior: Startup admission rejects symlinked `input_dir`/`output_dir`/`runs_dir`, DOCX archives are bounded by entry-count and uncompressed-size limits before parse/extraction, and the WMF parser enforces blob-size and record-count limits so malicious inputs fail closed.
features.residual_risk: PDF and XLSX parser surfaces still rely mostly on library-level limits and do not yet have the same document-specific admission thresholds as DOCX and WMF.

features.title: Operational security threat model
features.behavior: `docs/security.md` records the trust boundaries, threat classes, subprocess inventory, and font/path policies that govern untrusted document handling in the current product scope.
features.residual_risk: The threat model is an operational baseline, not a sandbox guarantee or a formal external security review.

features.title: Git-backed secret scan gate
features.behavior: `windows-ci` installs Gitleaks and runs `gitleaks git --config .gitleaks.toml --exit-code 1 .`, keeping default secret rules plus a narrow product-specific rule for env-style `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` / `FORMULA_RECOGNITION_API_KEY` assignments while allowlisting only known fake fixtures and `.env.example`.

verification.target: Create a temporary git repo with OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<canary> and confirm the same command exits non-zero.

features.residual_risk: The required check covers committed git content for the repository and intentionally does not substitute for workstation hygiene on untracked local artifacts or external release bundles.

features.title: Protected PR gate surface on main
features.behavior: `main` requires strict PR status checks `secret-scan`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit-tests`, `harness-validator`, `formula-benchmark-gate`, `document-package-validator` and `release-smoke`, while PR closeout must include feature/state/validation fields via the pull request template.

verification.target: Open a same-repo PR against main and confirm merge eligibility stays blocked until all required checks are green.

features.residual_risk: Required contexts are coupled to workflow job names, so any rename in windows-ci must be synchronized with branch protection on main.

features.title: Label-driven autonomous PR merge
features.behavior: `.github/workflows/autonomous-pr-auto-merge.yml` runs from `main` on `pull_request_target` and enables squash auto-merge for same-repo non-draft PRs labeled `agent:autonomous`, so merge completes automatically after all required checks succeed.

verification.target: Create a same-repo non-draft PR, add label agent:autonomous, confirm autoMergeRequest becomes non-null, and let the PR merge automatically after required checks succeed.

features.residual_risk: This proof must happen on a PR opened after the workflow already exists on the base branch; the bootstrap PR that first introduces the workflow cannot prove the path by itself.

features.title: Hosted nightly full e2e contour
features.behavior: A dedicated nightly workflow runs synthetic e2e, a full formula benchmark monitor, a CI-safe formula gate, repo-tracked table anchors, portable package build, EXE smoke and opens a diagnostic GitHub issue on failure with context from the latest merged PR.

verification.target: Trigger `.github/workflows/nightly-full-e2e.yml` via workflow_dispatch or schedule and confirm artifact upload or auto-issued GitHub failure report.

features.residual_risk: GitHub-hosted runners still cannot access the external D:\ corpus, so the full formula manifest currently runs as monitor-only without thresholds and the failure issue can fall back to head_ref/author for historical merges that predate the explicit PR template field.

features.title: Tag-driven release publication
features.behavior: A dedicated release workflow reacts to `v*` tags, rebuilds the portable Windows package, regenerates changelog-backed release notes, and publishes the zip plus checksum to GitHub Releases without a manual publication step.

verification.target: Push a `v0.x.y` tag and confirm `.github/workflows/release.yml` creates or updates the matching GitHub Release with the portable zip, checksum and notes rendered from `CHANGELOG.md`.

features.residual_risk: The code path is validated locally, but the first hosted proof still depends on a real `v*` tag push; stable tags intentionally fail if `CHANGELOG.md` does not contain an exact version section.

features.title: Pluggable formula provider chain
features.behavior: Formula-recognition postprocess no longer hard-codes backend/provider branching; it dispatches through a `FormulaProvider` protocol with `LocalTesseractProvider`, `OpenRouterProvider` and `NullProvider`, so fallback order is explicit data rather than orchestration-specific conditionals.
features.residual_risk: Formula providers are now abstracted, but the wider pluggable surface still depends on S3.2 for OCR and catalog writers, and live provider quality/cost remains an operator-triggered concern outside automated tests.

features.title: Machine-readable telemetry companion
features.behavior: Task-level validation and state-update signals are stored in a schema-backed JSONL companion with feature traceability, alongside the human-readable markdown telemetry log.
features.residual_risk: Historical telemetry remains primarily in markdown; JSONL starts as a structured companion from the latest harness iterations.

features.title: Machine-readable quality scorecard companion
features.behavior: Observed quality signals are summarized from structured telemetry and feature spine into a schema-backed scorecard companion, while the human-readable markdown structured companion section is kept in sync through a generated markdown check and can be consumed by the weekly eval loop.
features.residual_risk: Generated scores and markdown sync are proxy signals from telemetry coverage and still need qualitative interpretation in the weekly eval loop.

features.title: Generated weekly eval companion
features.behavior: Weekly eval can be refreshed in one command or via an optional Windows Scheduled Task helper from the machine-readable scorecard, structured telemetry and machine-readable sampled weekly reviews into generated JSON and markdown snapshots with coverage gaps, next actions and qualitative sampling evidence.
features.residual_risk: Weekly snapshot больше не purely proxy-only на reviewed weeks; schedule helper removes refresh overhead, but qualitative review scores in docs/agent-weekly-reviews.v1.json still require human/agent sampling discipline.
